key_insight: The paper replaces learned diffusion trajectory scores with analytical local scores built from obstacle, smoothness, velocity, and inter-agent constraints, enabling training-free motion planning.
engineering_relevance: This makes diffusion-style planning easier to deploy in new maps and multi-robot settings where demonstration data is scarce or unavailable.
method: Decompose the trajectory score into local interactions between neighboring waypoints and nearby constraints.
Use analytical terms for feasibility, smoothness, and collision avoidance instead of training a global score model.
Run iterative denoising to refine entire trajectories while preserving classical optimization structure.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on complex environments and large multi-agent tasks, including 300+ agents with 100+ obstacles, producing feasible paths in under 6 seconds on a GPU and outperforming strong baselines.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and completeness of the analytical local terms, so edge cases in constraint modeling or dense environments may reduce feasibility.
paper_title: Training-Free Diffusion Planning with Analytical Local Scores
